title: Even though it’s not legally required, I do think it kind of sucks th...
transcript: Here's something I think three people will care about, but I find it really fascinating. So I just saw it's a wonderful Life on Broadway, and I noticed in the playbill that despite being called it's a wonderful life, the playbill doesn't actually credit the movie anywhere. Instead, it credits the short story The Greatest Gift, which is the story the movie is based on. And I thought that's really weird, because it's using the movie's title, it's using the movie's script. How are they getting away with only crediting the short story? And it turns out that despite coming out after the short story, the movie is public domain, while the story is not. And that's because when the movie came out, it was a flop, so they never renewed the copyright And that's, in part, how it became a holiday classic. Networks Started playing it nonstop because it was free. And that's really when we saw this surge in popularity. And after the surge, we did see some attempts from the studio to get the rights back. And while some elements of the film do remain copyrighted, like the film's score, notably the script is not. Which is how it's able to be used here, because they're not using any of the copyrighted elements from the film. The added complication being that the underlying story of the greatest gift is still copyrighted. And so legally, they have to credit it in the playbill.
showTitle: It's A Wonderful Life: A Live Radio Play
classificationReason: Creator mentions attending the show, but the entire video is about playbill credits and copyright trivia — no opinion is offered about the production itself (acting, direction, experience). Classified as commentary.
